- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to cap the peak; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak (e.g., -0.70 → +0.29), model often underreacts; increase forecast slope or early-term values to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the first 5–7 days of a new 30d horizon; apply a 1–3% upward bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/–0.30), model tends to smooth too much; allow for 2–3% asymmetric noise in forecast to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
- If recent history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model often fails to recognize reversal; add a 2–5% upward bias in forecast 10–15 days ahead to anticipate mean reversion.
